text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- Former East German leaders Kessler, Streletz and Albrecht have to begin their prison sentences after supreme court rules that they can be held responsible for shoot to kill order at Berliln Wall and German-German border.

- German construction companies will have to pay minimum wage of 17 marks per hour in west Germany and 15.64 marks per hour in the east for all construction workers. Agreement will mean that foreign workers will no longer be able to be paid less than German workers.
- FDP parliamentary leader Hermann Otto Solms reelected head of party's parliament fraction.
HANDELSBLATT
- Eastern Germany will receive 28 million marks in support from EU in structural aid.
- Exports remain motor of German economy, rising five percent to 787 billion marks this year, according to German assocation of large and foreign trade (BGA).
- Bonn will make Eurofighter decision in early 1997.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl invites Russian President Boris Yeltsin to recover from operation in Germany.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Those who gave shoot to kill orders at the border can be held legally responsible, supreme court rules.

- Economic Ministry's Academic Advisory Panel urges introduction of three-step tax system in Germany and cutting the top tax rate to 30 percent. Tax rates should be 10, 20 or 30 percent based on income levels of up to 12,000 marks, 20,000 marks or 30,000 marks per year, respectively.
- Bavarian Finance Minister Erwin Huber says Bavaria will insist on additional controls to make sure convergence criteria are adhered to for EMU.
- CSU and FDP say that coalition row has ended. Solms calls dispute a "cleansing thunderstorm". FDP says it supports Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
DIE WELT
- Exports headed for record levels.
- Construction workers to receive minimum loan.
- Economic advisory panel urges radical tax reform
- Transport Minister Matthias Wissmann does not want to make cuts in spending for roads and rails.
